entries.text: Allah's Name to commence with, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Saad. (This is an individual letter of the Arabic alphabet; Allah and His Messenger know its exact meaning.) By the oath of this renowned Qur'aan.
Rather, the disbelievers are (caught up) in arrogance and are in opposition (to the Beloved Prophet Muhammad).
How many a generation did We destroy before them, so now they cry out, whereas it was no longer the time for escape.
And they were surprised that a warner came to them from amongst themselves, and the disbelievers said, 'He is a magician, a great liar.'
'Has he merged all the gods into One God? This is indeed something very strange.'
And their (Makkan) leaders went about (saying), that 'Leave him and cling steadfastly to your gods; indeed, he has his own (hidden) motive in this.'
'We never heard of this even in the latter religion of all; Christianity (that God is only One); this is just a new fabrication.'
(The disbelievers asked) 'Was the Qur'aan revealed (only) to him from out of (all of) us?' In fact, they are in doubt concerning My Book; rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
Are they the treasurers of the Mercy of your Lord, the Dignified, the Great Bestower?
Is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them for them (i.e. for the polytheists)? So, would they not just ascend using ropes?
This (group of disbelievers) is just one of the disgraced troops which will be chased away.
Before them, the people of Nooh had belied, and (the tribe of) 'Aad, and Fir'awn, the man of stakes (by which he used to torture the people).
And the (tribe of) Thamood, and the nation of Loot, and the People of the Woods (i.e. the dwellers of the forest); these are those (defeated) groups.
There is no one amongst them as such, who did not belie the Messengers, My punishment therefore became inevitable.
And they do not wait but for just one scream, which no one can avert.
And they said (mockingly), 'O our Lord! Give us our share (of punishment) quickly, before the Day of reckoning.'
Have patience upon what they say, and remember Our bondsman Dawood, the one blessed with favours; he is indeed most repenting (towards his Lord).
Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify (Allah) together with him, when the night falls and when the sun shines.
And the gathered-birds; they were all obedient to him.
And We strengthened his kingship, and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
And did the news of the claimants reach you? When they came into Dawood's Mosque, climbing over the wall.

When they entered the presence of Dawood, so he feared them, they said, 'Do not fear, we are two claimants, one of whom has wronged the other, therefore judge truthfully between us and do not judge unjustly, and show us the straight path.'
'This is my brother; he has ninety-nine female sheep and I have one female sheep; and he now says, “Give that one to me also,” and he pressurises me in this matter.'

Said Dawood, 'He is indeed doing injustice to you, that he demands your sheep to be added to his own sheep; and indeed, most partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do good deeds, and they are very few.' Thereupon Dawood realised this, that We had tested him, so he sought forgiveness from his Lord, and fell in prostration and turned (to his Lord).
We henceforth forgave him for this (act); and indeed, for him in Our Majestic Court is definitely special proximity and an excellent abode.

'O Dawood, We have indeed appointed you as (Our) vicegerent in the earth, therefore judge between the people with the truth, and do not follow desires which will lead you astray from Allah's path. Indeed, those who go astray from Allah's path, for them is a severe punishment for the reason that they forgot the Day of reckoning.'
And We have not created the heaven, and the earth, and whatever is between them in vain; this is the perception of the disbelievers. Therefore, for the disbelievers is destruction from the Fire.
Should We make those who believe and do good deeds equal to those who spread turmoil in the earth? Or should We equate the pious with the wickedly disobedient?
This is a Book which We have sent down upon you, a blessed one, so that they (i.e. people) should ponder upon its verses, and the people of intellect should accept advice (therefrom).
And We bestowed Sulaimaan to Dawood; what an excellent bondsman. He is indeed most repenting (to Allah).

When there were presented to him (horses) in the afternoon, that when poised, they hence stand on three legs and while putting the brink of the hoof of the fourth leg on the ground, (they) were very swift when running.
Therefore, Sulaimaan said, 'The love of these horses is dear to me, for the sake of the remembrance of my Lord.' He then ordered them to be raced until they vanished in a veil out of sight.
He then ordered; that 'Bring them back to me.' And he began stroking their shins and necks.
And We indeed tested Sulaimaan and placed a lifeless body (i.e. a miscarried baby) on his throne, (he) then returned (towards his Lord).
He submitted, 'O my Lord, forgive me and bestow upon me such a kingdom, which shall not be fitting to anyone after me. Indeed, only You are the Great Bestower.'
We henceforth gave the wind under his control, which would move steadily by his command, wherever he wished.
And made the devils; every builder and diver, subservient to him.
And other (devils) bounded in chains.
'This is Our Bestowal (O Sulaimaan), now whether you bestow favour (by giving) or withhold, you will not be held accountable at all.'
And indeed, for him in Our Majestic Court is definitely proximity and an excellent abode.
And remember Our bondsman Ayyoob (Job); when he called upon his Lord; that 'The Devil has afflicted me with adversity and pain.'
We said to him, 'Stamp your foot on the ground; this cool spring is for bathing and drinking.'
And We bestowed him his family and more similar to it (in number), as a mercy from Us, and advice for the people of intellect.

And We said, 'Take a broom in your hand and strike her with it (since you swore an oath to strike your wife with a hundred lashes), and do not break your oath.' We indeed found him patient, what an excellent bondsman. He is indeed ever repenting (towards Us).
And remember Our bondsmen Ibrahim, and Is-haaq, and Ya'qoob; the men of power and knowledge.
Indeed, We granted them distinction with a pure excellence, which is the remembrance of that abode (of the Hereafter).
And according to Us, they are indeed the chosen, the best.
And remember Isma'eel and Yasa' (Elisha) and Zul-Kifl; and they are all excellent.
This is advice; and indeed, the abode of the pious people is excellent.
Gardens for living; all the gates are open for them.
Reclining, they ask for fruits in abundance and (different delicious) drinks.
And they have such wives, who look towards no one except their husbands, (everyone is) of the same age.
This is what you are promised for the Day of reckoning.
Indeed this is Our sustenance, which will never end.
For them (i.e. the virtuous) is this, and indeed for the rebellious is an evil abode.
Hell, that they will enter therein; so, what an evil resting-place.
This is for them (i.e. the inmates of Hell), so that they may taste it; boiling hot water and pus.
And similar other pairs (of punishments).

They (the disbelieving leaders) will be told, 'Here is another group falling along with you (into Hell), which was yours.' They will say, 'Do not give them plenty of open space; they surely have to enter the Fire, let them be restricted therein also.'
The followers will say, 'Rather, may you not get open space; it is you who brought this calamity upon us.' So, what a wretched destination.
They say, 'O our Lord! Whoever has brought this calamity upon us, double the punishment of the Fire for him.'
And they say, 'What is the matter with us that we do not see the (poor Muslim) men whom we thought were evil?'
'Did we mock them (just for the sake of it), or did our eyes turn away from them?'
Indeed, this is definitely true; the quarrel of the people of Hell with each other.
Say you (O Beloved), 'I am purely a warner, and there is no one worthy of worship except Allah, the One, the Dominant upon all.'
'Master of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Dignified, the Most Forgiving.'
Say you (O Beloved), 'That is great news.'
'Of which you are negligent.'
'What did I know about the heavenly world (on my own accord), when they (i.e. the angels) were disputing.'
'Only this is revealed to me, that I am not but a clear warner.'
(Remember) when your Lord said to the angels; that 'I will create a human from clay.'
'Then when I make him perfectly and breathe into him a spirit from Myself, (all of you) should fall down in prostration to him.'
So, all the angels prostrated; every one of them, that no one remained behind.
Except Iblees (Satan); he became arrogant and (in the knowledge of Allah) he was amongst the disbelievers.
Said Allah, 'O Iblees! What prevented you from prostrating to the one whom I have created with My Hands (of power)? Have you become arrogant (now) or were you (always) amongst the arrogant ones?'
Said Iblees, 'I am better than him; You made me from fire, and You have created him from clay.'
He (Allah) said, 'Get out from Paradise, that you are rejected (i.e. the cursed one)'
'And indeed, My curse is upon you till the Day of Judgement.'
He said, 'O my Lord! If it is so, then give me respite till the Day when all will be raised.'
Said (Allah), 'So, you are amongst those who are given respite.'
'Until the known time of that Day.'
He said, 'By the oath of Your Honour, I will definitely mislead all of them.'
'Except Your chosen bondsmen amongst them.'
Said (Allah), So, the truth is this, and I speak only the truth.'
'Undoubtedly, I will definitely fill Hell with you and with those amongst them who will follow you; all together.'
Say you (O Beloved), 'I do not ask any recompense from you for the Qur'aan, and I am not of the fabricators.'
'That (i.e. the Qur'aan) is not but advice for the entire universe.'
'And you will definitely come to know of its news (as the truth), after some time (i.e. at the time of death or the Day of Judgement).'
